title: Incident Response
description: On-call practice, blameless postmortems, escalation judgment, and SRE-style reliability practice — distinct from observability's instrumentation focus.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can follow a runbook to detect and mitigate a scripted incident, and can keep a timeline that separates an observed fact from an unconfirmed hypothesis.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can triage a scoped, simulated incident from alerts, dashboards and traces alone, restore service before finishing root-cause analysis, and draft a blameless postmortem naming contributing factors rather than people.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently design an alerting policy — thresholds, burn-rate windows and routing — for a service, defend in writing which conditions should page a human versus stay silent, and make a correct escalate-or-hold call on an ambiguous simulated page.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can run point on a multi-signal incident with incomplete information, coordinate mitigation and status communication concurrently, and produce a postmortem whose follow-up actions are split across detection, prevention and response.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's postmortem or alert design, name any blame-shifting language or unverifiable claim in it, and teach the detect/mitigate/diagnose sequence to someone new to on-call.
